scope: 171 finite synchronous shared user-resource heads, independent origin/liveness/effect checks, supported callback composition and explicitly closed mixed capture boundary. This is not a self-review of included 170 Package code.
code_review: Types admits only shared Address<Managed<finite Copy Record>> user-resource heads and only actual Managed local borrowing; a Desc local, a Package field, ByteBuffer and mutable heads remain outside this profile.

Independent Verify reconstructs the exact nominal resource definition for head types and BorrowLocal, checks LIVE Managed responsibility, and permits Copy payload AddressField without permitting whole-head ReadAddress or WriteAddress.

Whole-module head discovery enables actual Desc Hold roots in head-free callees. buffer_effects::infer propagates direct Desc access and internal callback roots through every reachable ordinary-call edge to a bounded fixed point.
Descriptor callback effects reconstruct local capture roots from CFG input facts and update descriptor local state at every instruction. Ordinary helper argument names do not establish separation.

The final mixed Desc+Address callback combination is deliberately Unsupported in a module containing actual shared heads. This applies conservatively even when the Address captures an unrelated Copy flag; it is not a proven per-capture read/write contract.

All captures_descriptors call paths that activate the mixed gate are gated by head_windows. No-head historical mixed Copy-address/Desc callbacks remain supported, including a shared environment alias chain.

LLVM BorrowLocal emits zero-offset GEP of the original local; shared reborrows preserve that pointer. The nominal Managed record has its ordinary inline payload representation and the drop live flag is cleared before user teardown.

Head-valued returns and head-derived address returns from head-parameter functions, head capture, captured Managed head borrowing, ordinary head function pointers, and FFI heads remain explicitly outside this slice.

failures: Nested generic callable helper contracts already reject in Expand; final probe uses the existing single helper with ordinary shared environment aliases.

A default captured bool flag is Address<Bool>, confirmed in typed IR; together with Desc it correctly meets the newly declared mixed Unsupported boundary. Final pure-Desc effect probe moves its branch outside the closure, retaining runtime branching in the ordinary helper.
retained_reviewer_exploration.not_counted_again: 4 exploratory native runs repeated the final nested layout / projected last-use controls.

limitations: Mixed Desc/Address callback invocation inside any actual-head module remains conservatively Unsupported until per-capture effects are implemented.
No claim for general nested callable helper contracts, arbitrary address returns/capture, mutable or sealed heads, imported trait implementation solving, or runtime Store composition.
Linux x64 native evidence only; no performance, product readiness, or complete-language claim.
